transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-03-12
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Marissa Chen (Redwood AE); Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE); Sana Rao (Acme - Head of Security); Tom Nguyen (Acme - Platform Engineer); Priya Patel (Acme - IAM Admin)

Summary:
Customer wanted a focused review on SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, and how Redwood maps SCIM groups to RBAC roles for least-privilege. Also discussed certificate rotation, audit logs retention, data residency, and KMS integration for encryption-at-rest.

Topics:
- SAML metadata and signed assertions
- SCIM group sync and attribute mappings
- RBAC role matrix and least-privilege recommendations
- Audit logs, retention, and export
- Data residency options and customer-managed keys (KMS)

Transcript:
[00:00] Marissa: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Marissa, AE at Redwood, and with me is Diego from our security/infra team. How are you doing, Sana?
[00:12] Sana: Good, thanks. Appreciate you squeezing this in. We wanted to walk through SSO setup details and how Redwood handles provisioning and RBAC.
[00:23] Diego: Great, high level — Redwood supports SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM 2.0 for provisioning. We can do both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated SSO, signed assertions, cert rotation, the whole thing.
[00:35] Tom: Awesome. Our prerequisites are a bit strict — we need signed assertions, audience restrictions, not sure about RelayState handling, and we may want JIT (just-in-time) user provisioning or SCIM group sync depending on how you map roles.
[00:48] Marissa: Totally, we'll go end-to-end. Diego, can you cover the SAML metadata and cert rotation process first?
[00:52] Diego: Sure. We provide an SP metadata XML — ACS URL, EntityID, certificate thumbprint. On your side you upload the IdP metadata, or we can ingest it. We support cert rollover with overlap windows so you don't have downtime: you can configure the new cert and we accept both for a configurable period.
[01:10] Priya: Do you require signed AuthnRequests? Our IdP enforces signed requests and expects signed responses with the assertion.
[01:18] Diego: We support signed AuthnRequests and signed assertions. We validate signature, audience, recipient, subject confirmation method, and conditions time window. We also check the certificate chain if provided.
[01:30] Sana: What's the recommended audience value? Our standard is the SP EntityID.
[01:33] Diego: Use the EntityID in the metadata. We'll share the exact string in the SP metadata we send — that'll be in the follow-up.
[01:40] Tom: About RelayState — we plan to use IdP-initiated flows for some dashboards. Any limitations?
[01:45] Marissa: We handle RelayState and honor it in IdP-initiated flows, but just flagging that deep linking can be impacted by session length settings.
[01:52] Sana: Great. Switching to SCIM — does Redwood support group provisioning? We need group->role mapping for least-privilege.
[02:00] Diego: Yes, SCIM groups are supported. We can sync users and groups. There are two common mapping modes: map SCIM groups to Redwood roles directly (preferred for simple setups), or use SCIM for user provisioning and manage role assignments inside Redwood via admin UI or API.
[02:17] Priya: If we map groups to roles, what's the attribute you expect? Are you looking for member attribute as a list of user URNs?
[02:24] Diego: We accept groups with members as expected per SCIM core — 'members' contains value/display where value is the user id. We also support group schemas from Okta and Azure with id/externals. We'll share an example payload in the follow-up.
[02:38] Tom: Any rate limits on SCIM? We provision lots of users and churn is high.
[02:43] Diego: We do have soft rate limits to protect the system — default is 10 req/sec for SCIM endpoints per tenant, with burst support. For high-provisioning workloads we can increase limits or recommend bulk provisioning via CSV+API during onboarding.
[02:57] Sana: How do you handle group rename or deletion? We want to avoid orphaned roles.
[03:03] Diego: We reconcile groups on each sync — we do incremental updates and a full recon periodically. Group deletions can either remove assignments (if configured) or move users to a fallback role depending on your policy. We'll show the recon behavior in the RBAC doc.
[03:18] Marissa: On RBAC, Diego prepared a role matrix. Diego, could you summarize the least-privilege recommendations?
[03:23] Diego: Sure — we recommend three baseline roles: Viewer (read-only), Operator (manage routes/models but no billing or org-level). Admin has full org-level controls including billing and user management. For sensitive resources we support scoped roles per-project or per-model. Best practice: assign SCIM groups to least-privilege roles and use short-lived elevation for admin tasks via approval flows.
[03:46] Priya: Do you support attribute-based access control (ABAC) or just role-based?
[03:51] Diego: Primary model is RBAC with role hierarchies and resource scoping. We don't have full ABAC in the hosted product yet, but you can use tags and project scoping to approximate ABAC. For Private deployments we can discuss extensions.
[04:06] Tom: Audit logs — what events do you capture and how long do you retain them?
[04:10] Diego: We capture auth events (login, SSO assertion accepted), provisioning events (SCIM create/update/delete), role assignments, API key creations, model deploys, and inference errors. Default retention for hosted is 90 days in the Console. We can export to customer SIEM (Syslog/Datadog/Elastic) for longer retention.
[04:29] Sana: Do audit logs include the SAML NameID or is it anonymized?
[04:33] Diego: Logs include the internal user id and can surface the NameID if you enable PII logging for security teams. For strict compliance customers we turn on PII redaction by default and provide a separate secure export path.
[04:49] Marissa: On encryption — customers have asked about customer-managed keys.
[04:53] Diego: Hosted supports customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault for encryption-at-rest. Redwood stores a tenant envelope key encrypted with the KMS key. For Private deployments we can integrate with HSMs.
[05:05] Priya: Are there cross-tenant leakage risks when using shared infrastructure?
[05:09] Diego: We logically isolate tenant keys and data. In hosted, data is encrypted per-tenant and we use network isolation and tenant-aware IAM controls. For regulated workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[05:21] Tom: Data residency — can we choose EU-only region and make sure backups stay in region?
[05:25] Marissa: Yes, we offer region pinning for accounts and backup retention in customer region for the Dedicated/Private tiers; hosted accounts on our EU region follow EU residency. We'll confirm the level of guarantees and provide the data residency whitepaper.
[05:42] Sana: SOC2/ISO availability — do you publish certificates and when is the next audit?
[05:47] Marissa: We publish SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certificates on our compliance portal. Our last SOC 2 report is from Q4 2024 and ISO from early 2024. We'll share the secure link after this call.
[05:59] Tom: For SAML metadata exchange — what's the best practice for test accounts and rolling to prod?
[06:04] Diego: Create a test IdP app with a test org and a handful of users and groups. We recommend scoping the SP to a test EntityID and test ACS URL. Once SCIM and SSO validations pass, you rotate certs, then move to prod with a scheduled cutover and overlap window.
[06:20] Priya: On permissions mapping — if we have a devs group and they need model deploy rights only for staging projects, can we scope that?
[06:28] Diego: Yes — we support project-level RBAC. You can map group 'devs' to a role scoped to 'staging' project only. We'll include an example matrix.
[06:38] Sana: About least-privilege: do you have built-in periodic access review tooling?
[06:44] Diego: We have access audit exports and can schedule reminders via the Console; full automated access review workflows are on the roadmap. For now we support CSV exports for reviews.
[06:56] Marissa: Any questions on SCIM bulk operations? Priya?
[06:59] Priya: If we do bulk add thousands of users, do you provide idempotency tokens to prevent duplicates?
[07:05] Diego: Our SCIM endpoints support idempotency via externalId and we return 409 if a duplicate externalId is used incorrectly. We also suggest using bulk CSV import for large one-time migrations.
[07:17] Tom: How about SCIM group filtering? We only want certain groups synced.
[07:21] Diego: You can configure SCIM filters on the IdP side or configure group filters in Redwood during setup. We'll include filter examples for Okta and Azure AD.
[07:32] Sana: What about SSO sessions and session timeout? We need SSO sessions to expire after 30 minutes of inactivity.
[07:38] Diego: Session timeout is configurable per tenant; default is 24 hours but we can set to 30 minutes or enforce SSO session policies from the IdP with shorter sessions.
[07:49] Priya: Are there controls for admin elevation and approvals? We need approvals logged.
[07:54] Diego: We have role elevation via temporary access tokens and log elevation events in the audit trail. Approvals are supported via manual workflow; we log approver and reason.
[08:05] Marissa: A couple of nuanced questions we see in enterprise — certificate rotation automation, automated SCIM delta performance, and IP allowlist for SAML endpoints. Any special constraints from your side, Tom?
[08:16] Tom: IP allowlist is needed — we can only accept SAML traffic from a known set of IPs. Can you provide static IPs for your SAML endpoint?
[08:23] Marissa: We maintain published egress and ingress IP ranges per region and will share them. For Dedicated we can provide dedicated addresses.
[08:31] Priya: Regarding KMS integration — do you support customer rotation of KMS keys and automatic rewrap?
[08:36] Diego: Yes, we support key rotation in KMS; Redwood rewraps the tenant envelope key and rotates without downtime. We'll include a diagram.
[08:46] Sana: For compliance evidence — can we get a mapping of controls to SOC2 criteria?
[08:51] Marissa: Absolutely, we'll send a controls mapping document and a secure link to the SOC2 report.
[08:58] Tom: A question about metadata — do you support SHA-256 signatures only or SHA-1 too?
[09:03] Diego: We require SHA-256 for signatures. SHA-1 is deprecated and not accepted.
[09:09] Priya: What's your turnaround for security questionnaire items (e.g., SIG, CAIQ)?
[09:14] Marissa: For standard questionnaires we aim 5-7 business days; for lengthy enterprise packets we coordinate with our security team — usually 7-14 days depending on scope.
[09:25] Sana: If we wanted Private deployment, what's the difference in SSO/SCIM capabilities vs hosted?
[09:31] Diego: Private gives you more control: you can bring your own HSM, full Local AD/LDAP integrations, and on-prem network controls. Hosted has the same SAML/SCIM features but Private can extend ABAC and custom connectors.
[09:45] Tom: On encryption transport — do you support mTLS for SCIM endpoints?
[09:50] Diego: Yes, SCIM can be protected via mTLS in Dedicated/Private. For hosted we recommend TLS with mutual certs possible for enterprise customers.
[09:59] Marissa: Let's do a brief demo of the RBAC UI and SCIM mapping — Diego, jump in?
[10:04] Diego: Sure. (screen sharing noises) I'm opening the RBAC page. Here's a role 'Model Operator' with permissions to deploy and manage model versions but not billing. You can map a SCIM group to this role from the SCIM mappings panel.
[10:22] Priya: Looks good. Can we preview members that will be assigned before applying mapping?
[10:27] Diego: Yes, we have a preview showing sample matched users and a dry-run mode for SCIM mapping.
[10:36] Tom: Can we hook mapping changes into Slack for audit and approvals?
[10:40] Diego: We support webhook notifications and can integrate with Slack via your automation. Those events are also in the audit log.
[10:49] Sana: A small point: some of our auditing requires immutable export to an external S3 bucket. Do you support secure export?
[10:56] Diego: Yes, we can export logs to a customer S3 bucket with SSE-KMS and provide write-only credentials for the export lambda.
[11:07] Marissa: Ok, we're about halfway through, do you want to continue the deep dive or switch to Q&A?
[11:13] Sana: Continue for a bit more on SCIM and then Q&A.
[11:18] Diego: SCIM attribute mapping: we expect core attributes (userName, givenName, familyName, emails) and recommend externalId to map identities. For groups we accept displayName and members[]. For custom attributes we support custom SCIM schemas via extension.
[11:36] Priya: If our IdP uses uuid for user ids, is that ok?
[11:40] Diego: That's fine. We store the externalId and map it. The important part is consistency so SCIM updates match existing users.
[11:50] Tom: Can we partially provision via SCIM and manage other role assignments via API for exceptions?
[11:55] Diego: Yes, hybrid approach is common. SCIM for day-to-day provisioning and API/UI for ad-hoc exceptions.
[12:03] Sana: Any gotchas with group nesting?
[12:07] Diego: We don't currently expand nested groups in the SCIM sync. We expect your IdP to flatten groups or provide the membership you need. That's a known limitation; we document it and have workarounds.
[12:19] Priya: About SCIM error handling — do you retry on 5xx? Do you surface errors clearly?
[12:25] Diego: We queue and retry transient 5xx errors. For 4xx we return the error back to the IdP. We surface detailed error messages in the Console and in exported logs.
[12:38] Marissa: Recording a couple of decisions — we'll send the SP metadata and the RBAC matrix. Customer will provide a test IdP account and SCIM attribute mapping. Any final compliance questions?
[12:51] Sana: One last — can you share the contact for incident response and data subject requests?
[12:56] Marissa: Yes, our security ops contact and DPO details are in the compliance packet we'll share.
[13:05] Tom: Great. That covers most of it. Next steps?
[13:09] Marissa: I'll list those in the follow-up email. Thanks everyone.
[13:20] Diego: A few additional notes while we have the group — certificate lifetimes: we recommend rotating certs every 12 months and doing emergency rotation as needed.
[13:33] Priya: For emergency rotation, what's the process?
[13:36] Diego: You upload the new cert via Console or API and set the overlap period. If you need immediate cutover we can assist with a short maintenance window.
[13:48] Sana: For our security reviews we need a reproducible test plan. Can Redwood provide a checklist for SSO/SCIM validation?
[13:55] Marissa: Yes, we'll provide a checklist: metadata exchange, assertion validation, group sync validation, SCIM error handling, audit log checks, and performance/bulk test steps.
[14:06] Tom: Any recommendations for test user attributes to avoid PII exposure during testing?
[14:12] Diego: Use synthetic users with consistent externalId and minimal PII; we recommend unique emails like test+env@example.com.
[14:22] Priya: About the RBAC mapping demo — can you export the role matrix as CSV?
[14:27] Diego: Yes, exportable as CSV and JSON via the admin API.
[14:33] Sana: Are role changes versioned so we can audit who changed a mapping?
[14:38] Diego: Yes, mapping changes are versioned and recorded in the audit logs with actor and timestamp.
[14:47] Tom: For long-term retention we might want to push logs into our ELK stack — what format?
[14:52] Diego: We support JSON lines export with a documented schema. We'll send the schema in the follow-up.
[15:03] Marissa: Do you have any SSO caveats for legacy SAML implementations?
[15:09] Diego: If the IdP only supports SHA-1 or older bindings, that's a blocker. We ask customers to upgrade. For odd behaviors we support a troubleshooting session.
[15:21] Priya: If we set up SCIM with a filter, how do we test the filter without impacting production?
[15:27] Diego: Use the dry-run mode or apply filter to the test app in your IdP. Redwood will provide a preview of matched users.
[15:38] Tom: About export to S3 — can we use customer-managed KMS for that bucket and rotate keys?
[15:44] Diego: Yes, we support SSE-KMS using your KMS key and rotation is handled by your cloud provider. We just write encrypted objects.
[15:55] Sana: Any SLA on SCIM provisioning latency?
[15:59] Diego: We don't guarantee per-item latency but aim for sub-second for single operations and bounded processing for batches. For critical provisioning we recommend a pre-warm step.
[16:11] Priya: On the topic of data residency again — do you encrypt backups separately and can they be locked to region?
[16:18] Diego: Backups are encrypted with the tenant envelope key and stored in region for region-pinned accounts. For Dedicated we can provide contractual guarantees.
[16:30] Tom: For incident response — if there's a suspected exfil, what's the expected notification SLA?
[16:36] Marissa: We have an incident response playbook with notification windows; for high-severity incidents we notify customers within one hour and provide a status cadence.
[16:48] Sana: Will the incident notifications include forensic artifacts?
[16:52] Diego: We provide logs and IR artifacts as appropriate, subject to legal/forensics constraints.
[17:04] Priya: Do you do annual pen tests and share summaries?
[17:08] Marissa: Yes, we do annual penetration tests and will share an executive summary; deeper reports are available under NDA.
[17:19] Tom: Can you discuss multi-tenant isolation on a bit deeper level?
[17:24] Diego: Sure — logical isolation via tenant ids, data encryption per tenant, and kernel-level isolation for compute with seccomp/container boundaries. Dedicated provides hardware isolation.
[17:38] Sana: For SSO, any restrictions on NameID format?
[17:42] Diego: We accept persistent and transient; persistent recommended for mapping. We'll document supported formats.
[17:50] Priya: About SCIM delta frequency — how often do you poll or accept pushes?
[17:55] Diego: SCIM is push-based from the IdP. For reconciliation we run delta checks hourly by default.
[18:08] Tom: In the event of a user rejoin (deleted then re-added), how do you handle idempotency?
[18:13] Diego: If externalId is reused we match and restore previous assignments; if a new id is used it's treated as new. We recommend consistent externalId usage.
[18:25] Marissa: Ok, we're reaching deeper technical items — I'll pause and see if there are any blockers for moving to a pilot.
[18:32] Sana: No blockers, but we need the RBAC matrix and test IdP first.
[18:38] Marissa: Understood. Diego, anything to add on scaling SCIM?
[18:43] Diego: For scale we recommend bulk migration, increasing soft limits during migration, and using externalId for idempotency. We can assist with a runbook.
[18:55] Priya: For compliance, do you perform background checks on ops staff?
[19:00] Marissa: Yes, background checks and access controls for ops staff are part of our SOC 2 controls.
[19:10] Tom: One final question on live cert rotation testing — can we do a staged rotation during a maintenance window?
[19:16] Diego: Yes, we recommend staged rotation with overlap and a rollback plan. We'll help schedule it.
[19:28] Sana: Great. Anything else on audit log schemas?
[19:31] Diego: We'll send the schema; it includes event_type, actor_id, resource_id, timestamp, and raw_payload for forensic use.
[19:43] Marissa: Let's open for final quick Q&A — 10 minutes left.
[19:49] Tom: On SCIM, do you support partial attribute updates via PATCH?
[19:54] Diego: Yes, PATCH is supported for partial updates and is idempotent when using externalId.
[20:05] Priya: For temporary elevated sessions, what is the max TTL?
[20:09] Diego: We cap elevation TTL to 1 hour by default; can be configured shorter.
[20:18] Sana: Regarding the compliance portal — can we get read-only access scoped to our org to pull documents?
[20:24] Marissa: Yes, we can provide a secure portal link with short-lived access tokens.
[20:35] Tom: For log exports, can you sign exported bundles for tamper-evidence?
[20:40] Diego: We can provide signed manifests for exported bundles.
[20:51] Priya: Do you rotate service account keys automatically?
[20:56] Diego: We encourage short-lived tokens; service account keys can be rotated via API and we log key creation/deletion.
[21:07] Sana: If we need data subject access requests (DSARs) handled, what's the process?
[21:12] Marissa: We have a process in the DPO playbook; we'll include that in the compliance packet.
[21:23] Tom: For the follow-up, who should we loop in on Redwood side for implementation?
[21:28] Marissa: Loop me and Diego. I'll be your AE and Diego will be the SE owner during setup.
[21:38] Priya: Can we get a small test harness to validate SCIM payloads against Redwood?
[21:44] Diego: We'll provide sample payloads and a test endpoint.
[21:54] Marissa: Great, I'll capture those. Any final items?
[22:00] Sana: No, that's good. Thanks.
[22:05] Marissa: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items discussed.

Recap & Next Steps (verbatim):
- Redwood to share SP metadata, RBAC role matrix, IP ranges, and compliance docs (SOC2/ISO) — owner: Marissa — due 2025-03-14
- Customer to provide test IdP account and SCIM mapping — owner: Priya — due 2025-03-14
- Diego to prepare RBAC mapping example and SCIM sample payloads — owner: Diego — due 2025-03-19

Action items (shorthand):
- Marissa: send metadata + compliance links (2025-03-14)
- Diego: RBAC matrix + SCIM examples (2025-03-19)
- Priya: test IdP + attribute mapping (2025-03-14)

End of transcript.
